ybm_intro_consent@1.0/en-GB/self/standar.name: YBM introduction and consent

stem.text:
Yorkshire Brain Map School Workshop - Citizen Neuroscience - NotreDame

Thank you for taking part in this workshop.

In this study, we'll use a special tool called electroencephalography (EEG) to collect information about your brain. We'll put sensors on your head, and they'll record your brain activity. You'll also help collect brain data from another person. This new way helps us gather brain data quickly with help from people who aren't experts. The EEG headset should not feel uncomfortable, so if it does at any point, just let a member of the research team know. EEG is safe, pain free, and non-invasive.

In addition to EEG, we'll also ask questions about your life and how you feel. We made a list of questions that ask about things like who you are, how you feel, and how happy you are. We care about keeping your answers private so we'll give you an anonymous code so your answers stay confidential during the study.

Joining this study is your choice, and you can leave at any time with no problems. If you want to leave, please let a member of the research team or a teacher know.

Our study has permission from the School of Psychology Ethics Committee (Ethics Reference: PSCETHS-1449, Date of Approval: 5/6/25).

The questions you're about to answer should take about 10 minutes to answer. Please finish the survey quickly and carefully so we can stay on schedule. Thank you for joining our study! If you have questions or worries, please feel free to ask.
Please click to indicate you understand and agree to these statements and consent to take part.

text.text: I understand that anonymized results from this study may be disseminated through conference presentations, publication in peer reviewed journals, compiled as part of a report, used in future projects, included on institutional websites, presented in electronic theses and may be made available on online data repositories.
I understand that my name will not be linked with the research materials, and I will not be identified or identifiable in the report or reports that result from the research.

I understand that if I choose to withdraw my data by contacting the primary researcher within 24 hours of submission (up until {withdrawal_date}) that my responses will be removed from the dataset and not used for analysis
I understand that I am free to withdraw at any time without giving any reason and without there being any negative consequences
I have read and understood the information on the study presented above and have been offered the opportunity to ask the research team questions via email (m.faizah@leeds.ac.uk)
I agree to take part in this study

score.ehi_sf.provenance: EHI-SF laterality quotient as the mean of items scored 100..-100 (canonical right-first anchors; positive = right-handed). Veale (2014) classification cutoffs (left/mixed/right) to be added as a classify step after verification.

score.swemwbs.provenance: SWEMWBS raw total (all 7 items required, per standard guidance). The metric-conversion lookup step is intentionally absent until the licensed conversion table is filed and transcribed (then added as version 1.1.0).

score.sdq25_s.provenance: Standard youthinmind SDQ scoring (0-2 coding, reverse items 7/11/14/21/25, subscale proration >=3 items, total difficulties excludes prosocial). Verify against the youthinmind scoring sheet before approval.

score.rcads25.provenance: Ebesutani et al. (2012) RCADS-25 raw-score structure. Item-to-subscale allocation and official missing-data/T-score rules to be verified against rcads.ucla.edu materials before approval.

score.stai5.provenance: Zsido et al. (2020) STAI-5: sum of five 1-4 items. Verify no reverse-scored items against the publication before approval.

score.bisbas12_ybm.provenance: Raw sums in administered coding (1=very true .. 4=very false); outputs suffixed _raw to signal direction is NOT yet normalised. Carver & White (1994) reverse-scoring convention for this subset to be verified before approval (A-22).
